method: Every source_url was fetched with User-Agent yamadori-dataset-worker/1 (the worker's own): all 200 text/plain. approx_size_chars and extract_chunks come from the worker's own imported html_to_text + chunks_of (12,000-char chunks, 60-chunk limit), not a copy. Licences were read from each repo's licence file (copied verbatim to bench/recipes/licenses/) and matched against the GitHub API spdx_id; see bench/recipes/licenses/NOTICE.md for attribution lines and the commit read. Domains were validated against domains.DOMAINS at write time and no name collides with an existing bench/recipes/*.jsonl.
gaps_targeted: bench/recipes had no React-core corpus: r3f*.jsonl covers react-three-fiber only. Priority is React 19 (Actions, useActionState, useOptimistic, useFormStatus, <form action>, use(), ref as a prop, Server Components/Functions, React Compiler and the Rules of React, Activity, useEffectEvent), then the Effects/refs/state Learn pages, then TypeScript typing and app architecture.
operator_command: For each candidate: datasets.create(c['source_url'], name=c['name'], kind='recipes', source_name=c['source_name'], source_url=c['source_url'], licence=c['licence'], language=c['language'], domains=c['domains']). All four assisted fields are answered, so the running worker advances each dataset through fetch -> extract -> index with no clarify stop. dataset_id is the id create() returned.
